name: Theodore Roosevelt
role: 26th president of the United States (1901-1909); Progressive (Bull Moose) Party candidate (1912)
summary: A Republican-turned-Progressive who as president (1901-1909) and in his 1910-1912 New Nationalism backed strong federal regulation of corporations, labor protections, graduated income and inheritance taxes, conservation and direct democracy, including primaries, recall and a popular vote on some state court rulings. He was a firm advocate of naval and military strength, universal military service, American expansion and tutelage over peoples he judged less advanced, strict separation of church and state, and the full Americanization of immigrants in one language and one allegiance, and he held hierarchical views of race alongside a stated rule of judging each man on his merits.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The 1912 platform he led pledged minimum wage standards for working women to provide a living wage, and his Autobiography names opponents of minimum wage laws as reactionaries.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His administration won the Hepburn Act giving the Interstate Commerce Commission power to set railroad rates and broke up the Northern Securities combination, putting federal regulation over market outcomes while leaving big business in place.

reviewHistory.rationale: Held that the public welfare outranks market outcomes and that government must supervise business and set rates (railroads), while not opposing business as such.

regulate-corporations.rationale: As president he had the Justice Department break up the Northern Securities railroad combination, won the Hepburn Act on railroad rates and pushed through the Meat Inspection and Pure Food and Drug Acts of 1906.

reviewHistory.rationale: Demanded strong national regulation of interstate corporations by a federal commission; said corporate wealth must be under publicity, supervision and regulation, while accepting large corporations.

reviewHistory.rationale: Held that the executive may do whatever the Constitution and Congress do not forbid, and the New Nationalism was impatient of deadlock from divided powers; also opposed one-man rule and limited his own terms.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His record was mixed: he did little to preserve black suffrage in the South and discharged 160 black soldiers without trial after Brownsville, yet invited Booker T. Washington to the White House and appointed some black officials.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He said Americans are developing their own distinctive culture and civilization, whose worth depends on the determination to keep it distinctively their own.

reviewHistory.rationale: Held the crucible must turn out Americans of one American nationality, not dwellers in a polyglot boarding house.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Sought strict exclusion of undesirables and ratio limits on vessels but said we cannot have too much immigration of the right sort.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In his 1910 Nobel address he proposed a League of Peace of the great powers to keep the peace among themselves and prevent it being broken by others, by force if necessary, and developing the Hague tribunal.

free-trade.rationale: Platform denounced the Democratic tariff-for-revenue-only policy as leading to widespread industrial and commercial disaster and backed a protective tariff.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Wrote that outside powers have a sheer duty to interfere in massacres like those of the Armenians and defended the intervention in Cuba.

open-borders.rationale: He asked Congress to strengthen the laws excluding immigrants and to keep out every anarchist, every person of bad character and the physically unfit, so that American citizenship is built from sound stocks.

limit-growth.rationale: Platform said conservation must not retard legitimate development; resources should be generously used.

revolution-justified.rationale: His government supported the 1903 Panamanian revolution against Colombia with a naval blockade that kept Colombian troops from landing.

experts-over-public.rationale: He wanted an expert tariff commission removed from political pressure, yet insisted that the people, not judges, must decide for themselves what fundamental justice means in law: his words point both ways.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Called the inheritance tax a far better tax than income tax and urged a graduated inheritance tax on large estates.

basic-income.rationale: In the New Nationalism he said to help any man who stumbles, but that if he lies down it is a poor job to try to carry him: help is conditional on effort.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Platform: believe in a protective tariff that equalizes competition and warned that tariff for revenue only would cause industrial disaster; also wanted downward revision and a tariff commission.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He urged laws to stop the growth of absentee landlords and tenant-worked estates so that farmers own their land, but his platform held business concentration inevitable and necessary and only to be regulated: the evidence points both ways.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: His 1912 platform called the issue of currency fundamentally a government function whose control should be lodged with the government, not left to private agencies.

democracy-best.rationale: Defended popular rule, saying people are masters of their Constitution, but also warned about the quality of citizenship.

direct-votes.rationale: Platform urged initiative and referendum on the states and wanted more direct action by the people under proper safeguards.

right-to-secede.rationale: Praised the Union cause and said the men who fought in 1861 were right.

political-violence-never.rationale: His government backed the 1903 insurrection that separated Panama from Colombia, blockading Colombian troops.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said the nation that has lost the fighting edge is in a dangerous and ignoble position and praised war's manly virtues.

separate-church-state.rationale: He said there must be complete severance of Church and State, that public money must not advance any creed, and that the public schools must be non-sectarian.

military-superiority.rationale: Said the navy must be maintained and increased in efficiency and kept strong relative to other nations'.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He described the United States as an experiment in making a new nation out of divers race stocks, aiming not to imitate an older racial type but to maintain a new American type.

reviewHistory.rationale: Wanted a single American nationality formed by assimilating German, Irish and other immigrants, though his racial writings favored Anglo-Saxon expansion.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: He described the United States as an experiment in making a new nation out of divers race stocks, aiming not to imitate an older racial type but to maintain a new American type.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rejected Marxian theory as refuted and condemned class hatred as a basis of politics.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He said the thing to do for every man is to give him a chance to make his greatest contribution, not to push him up if he will not be pushed, and stressed equality of opportunity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Wrote that Indians never had real title to the land and the continent could not be kept as a game preserve for squalid savages (though later as president defended Indian land rights against fraud).

self-interest-moral.rationale: Condemned sordid materialism and pursuit of mere wealth as a measure of worth.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He told the Knights of Columbus that a republic cannot succeed unless its citizens put devotion to duty before the question of individual rights, and that undue prominence had been given to rights.

reviewHistory.rationale: Treated suffrage and citizenship as duties first; said no law avails without character and the duty of public service.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Called orthodox Marxian economic socialism an exploded theory and said profits of legitimate business are justified by public benefit.

taxation-theft.rationale: Argued for higher and graduated taxes as a legitimate government power over fortunes and bequests.

school-vouchers.rationale: He declared against any division of the school fund, any public money for sectarian purposes and any State aid to parochial schools, and for the public school system in its entirety.

national-self-determination.rationale: He kept the Philippines under U.S. rule rather than granting independence, while Cuba became independent.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He held that public help should give a worthy man a chance to show his worth, not carry the man who lies down and will not be pushed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Insisted on justice to both employers and workers, condemned class hatred, and framed reform as fair dealing between the two sides.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Favored women's suffrage as an equal right, yet platform backed special protections for women's work and he stressed motherhood as woman's primary duty.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Platform wanted Alaskan coal opened to development at once under government ownership and public coal and oil lands used under lease.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He said there is no room for hyphenated Americans, that immigrants must become Americans and nothing else, speaking English and renouncing every other allegiance, and that immigrant colonies must end.

reviewHistory.rationale: Said immigrants must Americanize in speech, ideas and loyalty, that there is room for one language only, and that hyphenated Americans have no place.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

national-mission.rationale: He believed that the exportation of American values and ideals would have an ennobling effect on the world.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Platform said both old parties had become tools of corrupt interests and described an invisible government linking corrupt business and politics.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: He wrote to the eugenicist Charles Davenport in 1913 that society has no business to permit degenerates to reproduce their kind or to permit the perpetuation of citizens of the wrong type.

reviewHistory.rationale: Wrote in 1914 that criminals should be sterilized and feeble-minded persons forbidden to leave offspring.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Advocated an active state: labor regulation, social insurance, trust supervision, conservation, and the executive as steward of public welfare.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He said each man is to be treated on his worth as a man without regard to the land of his forefathers or his creed, yet wrote of the conquest of savages as righteous and of inferior races: his words point both ways.

reviewHistory.rationale: Said each man should be treated on his merits and defended a square deal, but also wrote of racial hierarchy and dismissed aboriginal claims; views reportedly shifted late in life.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: He held that the public schools shall be non-sectarian and that no public money should advance any particular creed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Praised righteous war and called a war with savages the most ultimately righteous of wars; backed intervention and expansion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Preached the strenuous life of struggle and held that nations that avoid strife decline; described conquest by strong young races as the engine of history.

separated-powers.rationale: His New Nationalism was impatient of the impotence that springs from over-division of governmental powers and asked that the executive be the steward of the public welfare.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Platform sought to prohibit injunctions in labor disputes that would not issue otherwise, and in 1907 said some criticism of labor injunctions is warranted.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: In 1918 he wrote that the men who clamor for an early or negotiated peace with Germany, or seek to divide the United States from its allies, are acting as friends of Germany and therefore as enemies of the United States.

reviewHistory.rationale: In WWI called pacifists who supported Germany traitors and demanded unreserved national loyalty.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: After winning in 1904 he pledged not to run again, following the two-term precedent, and kept the pledge in 1908; in 1912 he sought a non-consecutive third term.

reviewHistory.rationale: Said limited terms check dictatorship and declined a third term in 1908, though he ran for a non-consecutive third term in 1912.

recall-officials.rationale: Platform urged recall of officials, and he asked that unfaithful public servants be removed easily and surely.

people-in-arms.rationale: He wanted universal military training but also a greatly increased regular army and navy with a regular reserve, not a citizen militia in place of the professional forces.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He called the owner-worked farm home one of the strongest political and social bulwarks and the best place to breed vigorous leaders for country and city alike.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He wrote of the advance of civilization over savagery as ultimately righteous and of the duty of advanced nations to lead backward peoples.

reviewHistory.rationale: Wrote of savagery versus civilization and the dominant world races, and held that advanced societies must lead others.

death-penalty.rationale: He wrote that he always felt impatient contempt for the effort to abolish the death penalty out of sympathy with criminals, and that no criminal who has earned death should be allowed to shirk it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: He named the circulation of indecent literature among the crimes for which requests for pardon only made him angry as governor and president.

minority-language-support.rationale: He opposed any school exercises in a language other than English and condemned a foreign government's plan to foster the Russian language among immigrants as antagonistic to American sentiment.

reviewHistory.rationale: Said there is room for but one language in this country, English.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He had an American collector take over Santo Domingo's custom houses so that its foreign debts would be paid.

reviewHistory.rationale: In Santo Domingo, ran the custom-houses so creditors were paid and revolution-driven debts settled; backed enforcement rather than cancellation.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Platform wanted currency control lodged with the government and protected from Wall Street, and opposed a privately controlled system.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Said property rights are subordinate to the community's right to regulate its use to whatever degree the public welfare requires.

collective-defense.rationale: In his 1910 Nobel address he proposed that the great powers form a League of Peace to keep the peace among themselves and to prevent, by force if necessary, its being broken by others.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Said it was right to reject the counsels of peace in 1861 for the Union.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Urged a graduated income tax of the proper type and graduated inheritance taxes.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: He said the sure way to ruin the nation would be to let it become a tangle of nationalities each preserving its separate nationality, and wanted no immigrant colonies or foreign-language institutions kept apart.

reviewHistory.rationale: Opposed hyphenated loyalties and insisted all immigrants become Americans and nothing else.

reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Called materialistic Marxian socialism an exploded theory and stressed character and moral awakening as essential to progress.

ban-cartels.rationale: His Justice Department sued the Northern Securities combination, which the Supreme Court ordered dismantled in 1904, though he otherwise sought to supervise rather than abolish large combinations.

reviewHistory.rationale: Said blanket prohibition of combination is futile, but urged strengthening the Sherman Law against agreements to divide territory or limit output and directed suits against trusts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Platform demanded restricting courts' power so the people hold ultimate authority on social-welfare law via a vote on state judicial decisions; kept federal Supreme Court review.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He kept U.S. rule over the Philippines, building a government of Americans assisted by Filipinos with an elected assembly, and ran Santo Domingo's custom houses.

reviewHistory.rationale: Said the US must train Filipinos for self-government and administered Cuba, Santo Domingo and Panama; called leaving the islands infamy.

reviewHistory.rationale: He kept U.S. rule over the Philippines, building a government of Americans assisted by Filipinos with an elected assembly, and ran Santo Domingo's custom houses.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

public-money-creation.rationale: Platform said issuing currency is fundamentally a government function, called issue through private agencies harmful, and opposed the Aldrich plan for leaving currency in private hands.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Argued that correcting evils through reform answers socialists and populists, and rejected Marx's predictions as falsified.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: He condemned bull-fighting because the torture and death of the horses is enough to blast the sport, and wanted every form of harmless wild life shielded.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A lifelong hunter, he accepted shooting game in legitimate numbers while condemning any sport built on the torture of animals.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Told the privileged that much has been given and much should be expected, and rejected the multimillionaire of mere wealth as an asset.

office-by-exam.rationale: As Civil Service Commissioner he enforced the civil service laws against party regulars who wanted patronage, and as governor refused to give the main patronage posts to party regulars.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: He called easy divorce a bane to any nation, a curse to society and a menace to the home, and asked that marriage and divorce be put under national law to end the scandals of lax State laws.

single-official-language.rationale: He wanted English and no other language used for all school exercises and named a common language, the English language, as the first essential of Americanization, condemning foreign efforts to keep other languages alive among immigrants.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: In 1915 he called any discrimination against aliens a wrong and said there should be no denial or limitation of the alien's opportunity to work and to own property.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: At the Sorbonne in 1910 he called the growth in luxury and love of ease evident and unhealthy, and in 1910 he warned against the triumph of a sordid and selfish materialism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: His government supported Panama's revolt against Colombia with money and a naval blockade, a single case.

corporate-influence.rationale: He said great special business interests too often control and corrupt the men and methods of government and must be driven out of politics, and his platform described an invisible government of corrupt business.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He held that unions and corporations alike must obey the law, writing in 1903 that no rule of a union could be permitted to override the laws he was sworn to enforce, and condemned lawlessness by rich and poor alike.

non-intervention.rationale: He announced the Roosevelt Corollary that the United States would intervene in Latin American countries with chronic problems, and took over Santo Domingo's custom houses.

religious-nation.rationale: He held it a cardinal sin against democracy to support or oppose a man because of his creed and said Catholics, Protestants and Jews stand on an equality as Americans.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He said the United States was governing the Philippines in the interest of the Philippine people themselves.

social-market-economy.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about regulation, competition or state direction, not a public safety net, which this statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: As president he regulated railroads, food and drugs, prosecuted monopoly and brokered the coal strike while treating big business as a natural part of a maturing economy he never sought to abolish.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about regulation, competition or state direction, not a public safety net, which this statement now asks about.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He wrote that if the great civilized nations completely disarmed the result would be an immediate recrudescence of barbarism, and likened disarmament to abolishing a city's police.

racial-franchise.rationale: He appointed black men to federal patronage posts in the South and refused to apologize when the South denounced it.

open-government-data.rationale: His 1912 platform pledged publicity of committee hearings except on foreign affairs, the recording of all votes in committee and the registration of lobbyists.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: His platform called the concentration of vast wealth under an unregulated corporate system a power insufferable in a free government, and he warned of a small class of enormously wealthy men accumulating power against the general welfare.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He described marriage as a partnership that should be one of equal rights, love and self-respect.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: He said no man should receive a dollar unless it was fairly earned and that every dollar should represent service rendered, not gambling in stocks, while not dismissing dividends.

family-wage.rationale: He said no man can be a good citizen unless his wage is more than sufficient to cover the bare cost of living, and that a man must be able to support his family.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He called wars with barbarous or semi-barbarous peoples a regrettable but necessary international police duty, and held that peace yields to righteousness when they conflict.

future-generations.rationale: As president he moved federal policy from exploiting natural resources to managing them, creating 150 national forests, five national parks, eighteen national monuments and 51 wildlife refuges.

arms-reduction.rationale: His platform favored an international agreement to limit naval forces, yet he warned that it would be wicked for the civilized powers to disarm and built two battleships a year: his words point both ways.

collective-bargaining.rationale: His 1912 platform favored the organization of workers, men and women, as a means of protecting their interests, and he wrote that he became a strong believer in labor unions.

farm-price-support.rationale: His 1912 platform pledged to foster agricultural credit and co-operation for farmers.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: He proposed that an alien who remains without learning to speak English for more than a certain number of years should be deported, and named a common language, English, as the first essential.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: In 1903 he ordered the reinstatement of a Government Printing Office foreman removed only for expulsion from his union, writing that no union rule could override the law.

premarital-sex.rationale: He urged a single standard of sex morality, early marriage and a strict sense of conjugal obligation to raise the standard of chastity.

women-suffrage.rationale: He wrote that voting is as much a right of women as of men and that he became a zealous adherent of woman suffrage; his 1912 platform pledged equal suffrage to men and women alike.

national-church-status.rationale: He held that there must never be any union of Church and State and that such union is partly accomplished whenever a given creed is aided by the State.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: His platform said natural resources are owned by the people and should stay in public hands, opened to use on terms giving the people a moderate return, with reasonable compensation for water power rights.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: As president he used the press as a bully pulpit to reach the people directly, bypassing political parties and machines, and took the Hepburn Act to the public over the Senate's resistance.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: In his annual messages he asked that all kinds of money be kept interchangeable and convertible at the holder's will into the established gold standard.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: His administration made the 1907-1908 Gentlemen's Agreement under which Japan restricted the emigration of laborers to the United States.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: In 1910 he quoted Lincoln that labor is prior to and the superior of capital, and said Lincoln took substantially the attitude we ought to take on capital and labor.

generational-constitutional-review.rationale: His platform said the people must use their sovereign powers in accordance with the needs of each generation and pledged an easier, quicker method of amending the federal Constitution.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: On his 1909-1910 African safari he took more than 3,000 animal trophies, including elephants, hippos, lions and rhinos.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: He preached not the doctrine of ignoble ease but of the strenuous life, the life of toil and effort, of labor and strife.

constitution-recognises-indigenous-natio.rationale: In his first annual message he said the time had come to recognize the Indian as an individual and not as a member of a tribe, calling the Allotment Act a mighty pulverizing engine to break up the tribal mass.

indigenous-internal-justice.rationale: He asked that the marriage laws of the Indians be made the same as those of the whites and that tribal funds be broken up into individual holdings.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: He urged a graduated income tax on big fortunes in 1910 and a moderate but progressive income tax in his later essays.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: He asked Congress for national power to deal radically and efficiently with polygamy, saying it was neither safe nor proper to leave it to the States.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: He wrote that universal suffrage had not made the Haytians able to govern themselves, and that the Filipinos were wholly unfit to govern themselves when the United States took the islands.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: His platform kept agricultural lands open to the genuine settler and to patent under the Homestead Law, reserving public ownership for forests, coal, oil and water power.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: He demanded that Germany and Britain submit their Venezuela dispute to arbitration and mediated the Portsmouth peace and the Algeciras settlement.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: He said allegiance must be purely to the United States, that any man of dual or divided allegiance would have been removed from his administration, and that the immigrant must renounce allegiance to every foreign government.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: His 1912 platform pledged legislation compelling strict limitation of all campaign contributions and expenditures, and he asked that corporate funds for political purposes be prohibited.

conquest-no-lawful-claim.rationale: He held that the settlers' conquest of the West from the Indians was ultimately righteous and that the Indians never had real title to the land.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Platform pledged social insurance against sickness, unemployment and old age and industrial accident compensation; also said he would not carry a man who lies down. notes: Second pass (rules 5): every book of his in the local library was searched by theme and cited or declined in booksNotUsed. His presidential record (antitrust suits, Hepburn Act, conservation orders, Panama, the Roosevelt Corollary and Santo Domingo customs, the navy, the Gentlemen's Agreement, the Brownsville discharge, appointments) is cited from Miller Center and State Department reports and from his proclamations and orders, and where it exists it answers the statement alone; his words answer the rest. Answers that rested on Wikipedia now cite the original (Americanism, 1915; the Davenport letter, 1913; the Kansas City Star editorials; the 1910 Nobel address). The New Nationalism is now cited from a full text rather than an excerpt. Race views are mixed in his own words (equal treatment by merit beside racial hierarchy) and are answered low. Themes searched: economy (trusts, tariffs, taxes, currency, labor law, unions), government (courts, recall, primaries, civil service, terms, executive power), world (Philippines, Panama, Latin America, arbitration, disarmament, the League, the First World War), society (immigration, language, religion, family, race, crime, prostitution, eugenics), ecology (conservation, wild life). Most statements on later topics (technology, the internet, gender identity, communist doctrine, decolonisation) have no record and stay null. The Outlook article 'Twisted Eugenics' (1914) was not found in an open full text; the 1913 Davenport letter is cited instead.
